title: Wild Mystics v3 — choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Capsule Station (gashapon capsule-toy packaging, at night). Keep it, adopt an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Capsule Station
options.lineage: Japanese gashapon machines, blind-box lineup cards and die-cut sticker sheets, lit at night
options.thesis: Every Mystic is a collectible: the UI is the capsule machine, the numbered lineup card and the sticker sheet, solid and outlined so it reads over any 3D scene.
materials: two-tone capsule plastic (element-coloured dome, ink base)
options.viewport: HUD: player capsule + party capsules top-left, a compass tape top-centre, a capsule-window minimap top-right, tracked quest as a mission sticker on the left, the centre third kept empty; magenta objective pins pop over every biome.
options.risk: Can tip into cheap toy clutter unless outline weight, corner family and halftone stay strictly rationed.

raised.raise: HUD law: the centre third stays empty, each corner owns one readout cluster, and the objective beacon snaps corner brackets onto its target.
Counts are physical events: gold, Aether, HP, XP and dex totals roll digit by digit when they change.
Rank is one variable: every selected, active or focused state rides one lift scale (flat → raised → popped) instead of ad-hoc styling.
Quest steps are numbered in a margin column and finished steps stay visible, stamped, never erased.
True press depth: every control travels 2–4 px onto a real contact shadow; nothing merely changes colour.
Sections part with deep gaps and colour blocks, never hairline rules.

options.label: Enamel Pin Sash
options.lineage: scout badge sashes and glossy hard-enamel pins
options.thesis: Every element, rank, sigil and Mystic is a hard-enamel pin with a metal keyline, pinned to a dark felt sash.
options.viewport: HUD pins in the corners, the tracked quest as an embroidered patch, the map as a felt sash of land badges.
options.risk: Familiar achievement-badge look; metal keylines drift toward the rejected gold filigree and dense lists suffer.

options.label: Viewfinder Bracket HUD
options.thesis: The island stays full-bleed; the UI is an OSD of corner readouts and snap-focus brackets.
options.viewport: Readouts pinned inside the safe-area corners, centre empty, brackets snap around the objective.
options.case: Fuses cleanly for the HUD but not for dense menus (team, dex, shop); creature-collector players do not identify with camcorders.
options.kept: Empty centre, one readout per corner, snap brackets on the objective.
options.risk: OSD caps over live imagery make dense stats hard to read.

options.label: Nixie Laboratory Counter
options.thesis: Quantities are the interface; every count glows as plasma in a glass tube.
options.viewport: Tube banks for gold, Aether and HP.
options.case: Only currencies and HP fit the metaphor; lists, portraits and maps do not.
options.kept: Every count change is a visible physical event.
options.risk: One-note; orange glow fights the fire element.

options.label: Cracktro Queue
options.thesis: One bitmap face riding baselines over a black void; rank is depth.
options.viewport: Menus as drifting baselines with no boxes.
options.case: Players do not identify with demoscene; unenclosed text fails over a bright 3D world.

options.label: Orizuru Fold Sequence
options.thesis: One sheet folded in numbered steps.
options.viewport: Quest steps as a numbered fold column.
options.case: Fits the quest log only; loses identification and whole-product clarity.
options.risk: Paper-craft calm clashes with battle energy.

options.label: Stitched Leather Studio
options.thesis: Menus as loved physical objects: tooled leather, linen, torn paper.
options.viewport: A leather journal on a shelf.
options.case: The fantasy-journal cliché this redesign is leaving; heavy textures cost phone GPU.
options.kept: True press depth on every control.
options.risk: Lands back in the rejected v2 register.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.thesis: Menus cut as blocks of cloud with blue voids between.
options.case: Light-first and abstract; neither identification nor clarity.

canonCard.label: Monster-collector standard
canonCard.thesis: Clean slanted panels, bright accent bars and a bold geometric sans, as the big creature collectors ship them.
canonCard.viewport: Corner HUD, slanted menu tabs, card grids.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
